transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-10 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ravi (Peregrine Head of Platform), Laura (Peregrine SRE), Tom (CTO), Nina (Oncall)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Maya: Quick recap, we had long tail evictions last Wed during a big batch job, customers saw timeouts and fallback to CPU route. We suspected KV cache thrash and a burst concurrency pattern, plus a mis-sized per-tenant cache. Agreed temporary "safemode" that reduces concurrency and routes to a smaller model instance; also need a sheriff/oncall rotation and updated runbook.

Transcript body:
[00:00:03] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight, 45 minutes is the plan. um who wants to kick off from the peregrine side, ravi?
[00:00:10] Ravi: yeah thanks maya we just want to make sure we have a clear ownership and a short term mitigation. last thursday's window was rough. thousands of requests saw 5-10s extra latency then timeouts, then our fallback caused duplicate downstream hits.
[00:00:24] Laura: yep, and from SRE perspective the eviction rate on the KV cache spiked. we saw keys with extremely high churn - some chats with long context kept rewriting the prefix. looks like our prefix shaping is bad.
[00:00:38] Ethan: to confirm, the borderline was an OOM eviction in the KV cache on the serving node, right? the runtime evicted the KV pages which then amplified recompute and made the tail worse.
[00:00:48] Laura: correct. the nodes hit memory pressure at pretty normal request volumes because several tenants used large prompts simultaneously. and the continuous batching amplified live set size.
[00:00:59] Tom: just to add, we run mixed criticality traffic - low priority analytics jobs spike nightly and collide with low-latency user traffic. they all land on the same pool.
[00:01:12] Maya: okay, so a few levers - isolate pools, change eviction policy, reduce concurrency, or use a safemode fallback to a smaller model that's cheaper to rewarm. longterm we prefer isolation, but short term we need an oncall empowerment and a safemode.
[00:01:29] Nina: about oncall, who becomes the 'sheriff' for this service? if there's a daily spike we need someone empowered to flip safemode.
[00:01:38] Ravi: we can do a rotation but need clear runbook steps so the oncall can act without escalation.
[00:01:44] Ethan: right. i'll propose a minimal safemode: detect sustained eviction rate > 0.5% for 3 minutes OR average latency delta > 40% for 2 minutes -> reduce concurrent request slots by 50% on the pool and route new requests to a quantized smaller model variant (quantized-8b) we have in the catalog. that should reduce memory pressure and rewarm costs.
[00:02:04] Laura: couple clarifications — is the smaller model compatible for all endpoints? some of our routes expect structured output.
[00:02:12] Maya: good point. it will be opt-in per route. the safemode will only be enabled for routes marked 'best-effort'. for strict routes we'll do backoff+retry not model swap.
[00:02:23] Ravi: pricing, will safemode cause a big cost delta? we need to know so we can accept the tradeoff.
[00:02:29] Maya: actually safemode should reduce per-token cost since you're on a smaller model, but there is an overhead from fallback orchestration. net should be lower, but we'll quantify and send a delta.
[00:02:37] Priya: i'll own sending the draft pricing delta and the runbook template. maya will piggyback with SLA language.
[00:02:45] [00:02:49] Ethan: quick note on root cause. the eviction pattern looks correlated with a specific tenant job that runs every 24h and creates large contexts. but the kernel of the issue is skewed key distribution - a handful of very hot keys evict many other entries. our serving runtime's continuous batching doesn't isolate hot-key flows today.
[00:03:08] Laura: yeah we saw the APS metric - almost 70% of cache churn was from ~0.7% of keys.
[00:03:16] Tom: is there a quick config we can flip to protect hot keys? something like per-key max entries or LRU windowing?
[00:03:22] Ethan: we have a knob for per-tenant cache cap and hot-key throttles in our dedicated offering, but it's off by default for the hosted pool. we can enable a soft cap in the pool config that will treat a single key's working set as limited. that'll buy headroom.
[00:03:36] Nina: will that affect correctness?
[00:03:38] Ethan: might increase recompute for that tenant, but overall cluster health improves. it's a degradation vs availability tradeoff.
[00:03:45] [00:03:50] Ravi: operationally we need the oncall steps: detect -> set safemode -> notify -> run eviction replay -> revert. can we write that down?
[00:03:58] Maya: yes, i'm scribbling a runbook now. step 1: confirm eviction spike via /metrics/evictions and /metrics/kv-miss. step 2: optionally flip pool to 'reduced concurrency' via console toggle or API. step 3: set safemode (route to quant-8b) for best-effort routes. step 4: notify downstream teams and start eviction replay in staging. step 5: if stable for 20m revert.
[00:04:22] Laura: can we automate detection thresholds so human flip isn't always needed?
[00:04:26] Ethan: yes we can add an automated policy but for initial rollout we prefer manual so the sheriff can judge impact. automation can be staged later.
[00:04:34] [00:04:45] Maya: question from redo, is there any compliance concern with safemode model change for audit logs? ravi?
[00:04:52] Ravi: no regulatory impact; we just need audit trails of who flipped safemode. we'll keep an audit event and require a ticket for permanent changes.
[00:05:00] Tom: about the eviction replay Ethan mentioned - can you outline what that entails?
[00:05:06] Ethan: the replay is a synthetic run of the same traffic patterns from logs to a staging pool instrumented with detailed KV traces. we will measure eviction rates, tail latency, and memory watermark. it's essentially a repro with tracing enabled.
[00:05:18] Laura: timeline for that?
[00:05:20] Ethan: i can run the replay by friday - need logs and the exact job signature from their analytics job.
[00:05:26] Maya: okay add that as action item.
[00:05:30] [00:05:45] Nina: can we define the sheriff rota? i volunteer for weekends but not weekdays.
[00:05:50] Ravi: let's do a two-weekly rotation; the first point of contact is Nina for weekends and Laura for weekdays, with ravi as escalation.
[00:05:59] Maya: good, we'll add that to the runbook and also to our status page incident page template.
[00:06:05] [00:06:25] Ethan: technical caveat — switching to quant-8b reduces memory pressure but increases mismatch risk for structured outputs. To mitigate, we will run a quick eval harness in staging to verify field-level integrity for the main routes before enabling safemode for them.
[00:06:41] Laura: okay, so opt-in routes only, we get it.
[00:06:44] Tom: what about longer term fixes?
[00:06:46] Ethan: longer term options: dedicated pools for heavy tenants, smarter KV eviction policy (hot-key capping), or adaptive batching that detects hot-key flows and isolates them. each has different cost/risk. dedicated pools are the cleanest but require commitment.
[00:07:00] Maya: for the commercial thread - dedicated pools or reserved capacity is probably the recommendation if they want consistent tail latency. maya note: sales follow-up.
[00:07:08] Ravi: we need numbers. if we do dedicated what is the ballpark cost increase?
[00:07:12] Maya: i'll run a delta and include a break-even on reduced incidents.
[00:07:17] [00:07:30] Priya: i'll coordinate the pilot and help with the contact points and timeline.
[00:07:33] Nina: real world test question - if safemode flips, what is the customer-visible degradation? approx percent?
[00:07:40] Ethan: expectation is smaller model might hallucinate slightly more on some rare prompts, and structured output might need post-processing, but p99 latency should improve. visible degrade for most users should be a modest change in response quality for best-effort flows.
[00:07:55] Laura: can we add a telemetry tag on responses served in safemode so downstream analytics can filter?
[00:08:00] Maya: absolutely — we'll add a response header and event.
[00:08:05] [00:08:20] Ravi: can we briefly cover rollback and safety net? if safemode makes things worse, how fast can we revert?
[00:08:26] Ethan: revert is immediate via API toggle. we recommend a 20m stability window; but if severe regression occurs, revert and escalate.
[00:08:35] Tom: will reverting reintroduce evictions immediately? possibly, but we should then do incremental adjustments like per-tenant caps.
[00:08:43] [00:08:50] Maya: ok nearing the end here, quick recap and owners. Ethan will run the eviction replay and share traces by 2026-07-17. Laura will provision staging safemode by 2026-07-14. Maya/Priya will share the runbook and pricing delta by 2026-07-13. Ravi to confirm sheriff rota by 2026-07-20.
[00:09:12] Ravi: sounds good. one last ask, can Redwood join the first oncall flip as a warm handoff?
[00:09:18] Maya: yes, we'll be available and Ethan will watch the replay.
[00:09:22] Nina: thanks all.
[00:09:25] Maya: thanks, we'll send notes and next steps.
